title: How's the novel
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The tech asks how the novel's going. Wood says he started. The tech says page one? Page one. The tech says that's the hard one. Wood says they're all page one. The tech says that's the hard one too.

panels.composition: The print shop. The TECH at the machine. WOOD with the week's strips. BARNABY on the counter.

image.prompt: a print technician at a large copier speaking to a young man with a stack of strips and a small dog on the counter, black and white, no words
a young man's face, guarded, black and white, no words
a print technician's face, dry, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The copier's light. Neither talking. The strip going under the glass is not about the novel; it's about a dog and a pot. The strip knows what it is.

image.prompt: a photocopier's green light sweeping over a comic strip about a dog and a stockpot while two men stand in silence, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: 'They're all page one.' The strip knows what it is; the novel doesn't.
